subject.title: fix(security): close Host-header Origin spoof bypass in gateway browser origin check

question: Should OpenClaw immediately remove implicit private-host same-origin trust for non-local gateway clients and require explicit allowlisting or the existing dangerous fallback for those deployments?
rationale: The patch changes a security boundary and can require action from remote or reverse-proxy operators; source review supports the direction, but maintainers should explicitly accept the compatibility posture after seeing real gateway behavior.

options.title: Land with explicit-origin migration
options.body: Require proof for both the blocked spoof path and an explicit `allowedOrigins` remote connection, then merge the fail-closed guard.

options.title: Preserve implicit remote private-host trust
options.body: Keep the existing behavior temporarily, accepting the reported Host-derived origin trust exposure while a broader migration is designed.

recommendation.title: Land with explicit-origin migration
recommendation.body: Require proof for both the blocked spoof path and an explicit `allowedOrigins` remote connection, then merge the fail-closed guard.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior browser-origin enforcement history makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the security-boundary decision.
